test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A man spends 83\% of his income. If his income increases by 23\% and his expenditure increases by 13\% , find the percentage increase in his savings.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Savings : Expenditure = 17 : 83 (Total Income = 100)

Net Change × Total = (S% × S-ratio) + (E% × E-ratio)

23 × 100 = (x × 17) + (13 × 83)

2300 = 17x + 1079 ⇒ 17x = 1221 ⇒ x = 71.82%

**∴ The correct answer is 71.82%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expenditure = 83% of Income

Income increase = 23%

Expenditure increase = 13%

**Formula:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Increase = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53899277cf33c34fd5b50eb1a7176728b799f9b1747d82b6a082fc65a588a6a3.png] 

⇒ Let Initial Income = ₹100

⇒ Initial Expenditure = ₹83 and Initial Savings = 100 − 83 = ₹17

⇒ New Income = 100 + 23% of 100 = ₹123

⇒ New Expenditure = 83 + 13% of 83 = 83 + 10.79 = ₹93.79

⇒ New Savings = 123 − 93.79 = ₹29.21

⇒ Increase in Savings = 29.21 − 17 = ₹12.21

⇒ Percentage Increase = (12.21 ÷ 17) × 100 = 71.8235... ≈ 71.82%

**∴ The correct answer is 71.82%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Balance

Income is always the sum of Expenditure and Savings. Any change in Income must be balanced by the sum of changes in Expenditure and Savings: ΔI = ΔE + ΔS.

Percentage Increase Formula

The percentage change is calculated as: % Change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100.

Weighted Average Application

In problems involving components, Total % Change = (w₁r₁ + w₂r₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂), where w is the weight (initial value) and r is the rate of change.
